gap: No result ChatGPT got states each screen's pixel density against the 15-inch Air's own 224 ppi (1080p screens land at 141-156 ppi, 63-70% of the Air; the 16-inch 2560×1600 Duex Float 2 Pro at 189 ppi, 84%), or what a bus-powered screen's watts do to the Air's 66.5 Wh battery (ASUS's 6.64 W for the ZenScreen MB16ACV is 1.5 times the Air's own average draw in Apple's web test, taking about 15 h to about 6 h by arithmetic).
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's best portable monitors for Mac, thisUSB's best portable monitors, WorkCocoon's extenders for MacBook Air, and Dealectric's own best-laptop-screen-extender and under-$300 pages, all opened 2026-11-26. None gives a ppi figure for any screen or for the Air. Macworld says only that the Trio 3 Pro 'is not as sharp and clear as the MacBook's own', and WorkCocoon explains density as a concept with no numbers. None compares brightness with the Air's 500 nits or weight with the Air's 3.3 lb. thisUSB lists watts for other monitors and says 'the laptop battery drains faster' but gives no hours. The per-chip external display limits are already on thisUSB and on our pages, so that part is not new. Standout is 2 rather than 3 because the Mobile Pixels store returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, so the watt and weight rows for our own picks rest on pages other than the maker's.
decides: It confirms the split ChatGPT made and puts numbers on it. On sharpness the Duex Float 2 Pro (189 ppi, 84% of the Air) beats the Duex Max DS (156 ppi, 70%) and the ZenScreen MB16ACV (141 ppi, 63%); only the 4K espresso Pro (282 ppi) exceeds the Air. The Float 2 Pro pays for that in weight: Macworld's 2.9 lb is 88% of the Air's 3.3 lb. Every 1080p row should carry the footnote that it is roughly two-thirds of the Air's density and 50-60% of its brightness. Lead to check: our record lists the Mobile Pixels Fold 16 QHD at the same 16-inch 2560×1600 (so the same 189 ppi) for $80 less than the Float 2 Pro and freestanding, but at 220 nits (44% of the Air). If the maker page confirms that, it is the sharp-text pick for desk use and a row we can link.

findings.label: Baseline: display, size, weight, battery
findings.value: 15.3-inch, 2880×1864 at 224 ppi, 500 nits; 13.40 in wide × 9.35 in deep; 3.3 lb (1.51 kg); 66.5 Wh; up to 18 h video streaming, up to 15 h wireless web
findings.note: Apple's figures. 66.5 Wh ÷ 15 h = 4.43 W average draw in Apple's web test; 66.5 Wh ÷ 18 h = 3.69 W in its video test.

findings.label: External displays the laptop drives
findings.value: Up to two external displays, with the built-in display on at full native resolution
findings.note: Apple: 'Simultaneously supports the built-in display at full native resolution'.

findings.label: External displays the laptop drives
findings.value: One with the lid open; a second only with the lid closed
findings.note: Apple: 'Close the MacBook Air lid to use a second external display with up to 5K resolution at 60Hz'. Same 224 ppi, 500 nits, 3.3 lb and 66.5 Wh as the current model. An extender attached to the lid cannot be used with the lid closed, so two added screens on an M3 need a display driver.

findings.label: External displays the laptop drives
findings.note: Apple: 'One external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz'. Same 15.3-inch 224 ppi panel, 3.3 lb, 66.5 Wh, 18 h / 15 h.

findings.label: Maker specs
findings.value: 15.6-inch, 1920×1080, 250 cd/m² typical, 6.64 W power consumption, 0.9 kg (1.98 lb) net, 35.8 × 22.5 × 1.0 cm; only video input is USB-C with DP Alt Mode
findings.note: The page does not say whether the net weight includes the stand or sleeve, and does not mention macOS or a driver. Native video path: one video-capable USB-C port.

findings.label: Normalised to the 15-inch Air
findings.value: 141 ppi (63% of the Air's 224); 250 nits (50% of 500); 1.98 lb (60% of 3.3 lb, on the desk, not on the lid); 35.8 cm wide against the Air's 34.04 cm
findings.note: ppi = √(1920² + 1080²) ÷ 15.6 = 2202.9 ÷ 15.6 = 141.2. Air figures from apple.com/macbook-air/specs read the same day.

findings.label: Battery cost on the Air, by arithmetic
findings.value: 6.64 W is 1.5 times the Air's 4.43 W web-test average; about 6.0 h instead of 15 h (web), about 6.4 h instead of 18 h (video)
findings.note: 66.5 ÷ (4.43 + 6.64) = 6.0 h; 66.5 ÷ (3.69 + 6.64) = 6.4 h. This is an estimate from ASUS's stated consumption and Apple's battery figures, not a test; it assumes the screen runs off the Air with no charger and ignores the extra GPU load.
